lines.en: Clara, my morning was awful. We had to wait two hours for the bus because of a breakdown on the highway.
lines.pt: Clara, minha manhã foi um desastre. Tivemos que esperar duas horas pelo ônibus por causa de uma pane na estrada.

lines.en: Two hours! Did you have to call your manager, or did he already know about the traffic?
lines.pt: Duas horas! Você teve que ligar para o seu gerente, ou ele já sabia do trânsito?

lines.en: I did not have to call him, luckily. He sent a message first, saying that nobody had to arrive before eleven.
lines.pt: Eu não precisei ligar para ele, felizmente. Ele mandou uma mensagem antes, dizendo que ninguém precisava chegar antes das onze.

lines.en: That was kind of him. Last winter I had to walk to the office in the rain, and I was soaked.
lines.pt: Foi gentil da parte dele. No inverno passado tive que andar até o escritório na chuva e fiquei encharcada.

lines.en: Terrible. At least you did not have to pay for a taxi, which would have cost a fortune in this city.
lines.pt: Terrível. Pelo menos você não teve que pagar um táxi, que custaria uma fortuna nesta cidade.

lines.en: True. Did the driver have to give the passengers a refund, or did the company just apologize?
lines.pt: Verdade. O motorista teve que devolver o dinheiro dos passageiros, ou a empresa só pediu desculpas?

lines.en: Nobody got a refund. We had to show our tickets, and then they gave us a voucher for the next trip.
lines.pt: Ninguém recebeu reembolso. Tivemos que mostrar as passagens, e então nos deram um vale para a próxima viagem.

lines.en: Well, a voucher is better than nothing. Are you going to use the bus again tomorrow, or will you drive?
lines.pt: Bem, um vale é melhor que nada. Você vai usar o ônibus de novo amanhã, ou vai dirigir?

lines.en: I will take the bus, but I think I will leave sooner. I do not want to be late for the report.
lines.pt: Vou pegar o ônibus, mas acho que vou sair mais cedo. Não quero me atrasar para o relatório.

lines.en: Good idea. As students, we never had to worry about schedules, and now everything depends on timing.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Como estudantes, nunca tínhamos que nos preocupar com horários, e agora tudo depende do tempo.

lines.en: So true. Let us meet here tomorrow, and if the bus is late again, we will complain together at the office!
lines.pt: Verdade mesmo. Vamos nos encontrar aqui amanhã, e se o ônibus atrasar de novo, reclamamos juntos no escritório!

facts.label: Obrigação no passado
facts.sub: We had to wait. I did not have to call. Did you have to pay?

facts.label: had to + verbo base
facts.sub: Had to é o passado de have to e expressa obrigação no passado: We had to wait two hours. Use sempre o verbo base depois: had to call, had to walk. Must não tem passado.

facts.label: did not have to
facts.sub: Didn’t have to diz que algo não era necessário, mas não proibido: I didn’t have to call him. Não confunda com mustn’t, que é proibição. Depois de didn’t, use have to.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Had to is the past of have to.
We say “I must wait” for the past.
items.why: Must has no past form; we use had to.

items.s: Didn’t have to means it was not necessary.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Had to is the past of have to. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I must wait” for the past. → Falso (Must has no past form; we use had to.)
Didn’t have to means it was not necessary. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A long wait at the bus stop · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cloudy morning in Houston. Felix stands at the bus stop with his bag. The timetable says the bus comes at eight. Clara arrives with two cups of coffee. They look at the empty road.

“Clara, my morning was awful. We had to wait two hours for the bus because of a breakdown on the highway.” says Felix. “Two hours! Did you have to call your manager, or did he already know about the traffic?” says Clara. “I did not have to call him, luckily. He sent a message first, saying that nobody had to arrive before eleven.” says Felix.
